primary_claim: SONAR text autoencoders implicitly represent correctness with a clear domain hierarchy: code validity (96% test accuracy) > grammaticality (93%, cross-lingual) > basic arithmetic addition (76%) > chess syntax (weak) > chess semantics (absent, at baseline), suggesting correctness understanding emerges from compression efficiency rather than explicit reasoning

effect.value: code validity 96%, grammaticality 93%, arithmetic (addition) 76%, chess legality weak/context-dependent, chess semantics at or below majority-class baseline

stated_future_work: non-linear probing methods for chess and other domains
limitations_stated: only one week; limited to two analysis methods (PCA + logistic regression)
notion of chess understanding may differ from model's internal representations; non-linear board state encoding could exist
didn't explore other correctness domains like logical reasoning, factual accuracy, or causal relationships
linear probes can sometimes find spurious patterns
quote: Turns out they do, but with a clear hierarchy: code validity (96% accuracy) > grammaticality (93%, cross-lingual) > basic arithmetic (76%, addition only) > chess syntax (weak) > chess semantics (absent).
